chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition (of marriage) except that which nourishes the flesh and the blood.
ai.seo_question: What amount of breastfeeding is required to make marriage prohibited between the nurse and the nursed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the criterion for *mahramiyyah* through breastfeeding, specifying that only milk sufficient to nourish the body and produce flesh and blood creates the prohibition. This definition is central to Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between mere sucking and substantial nourishment, and is often discussed in contrast to the Sunni view which may rely on a specific number of feedings. The emphasis on physical development underscores the biological basis of the kinship bond in Islamic law.
